1

 Judgment

This Civil Miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded in M.C.O.P. No. 09 of 2013, dated 06.06.2017 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, IV Additional District Court, Bhavani.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, IV Additional District Court, Bhavani
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred herein according to their litigative status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. The case of the claimant is that on 29.06.2012 at about 8:45PM, the deceased Anandakumar travelled in a Tavera Car bearing Registration No. TN-66-E-9927, which was driven by one Senthilkumar from Salem to Kovai N.H.47 main road, when they reached Chithode bye pass road,
near Saravana Hotel, a lorry bearing Registration No. TN-33-BA- 6945 belongs to the second respondent, driven by the first respondent in rash and negligent manner came in the opposite direction hit against the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Tavera car and resulted in accident.
Due to the accident, the deceased Ananda Kumar sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries on the spot.

A criminal case was also registered against the driver of the lorry u/s. 279, 337, 304(A)
of I.P.C.

The claimants has stated that the deceased Ananda Kumar was working as a Training Consultant in Focus Academy for Carrier Enhancement (FACE) and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month and the deceased was also got an offer letter as a Programme Analyst Trainee from Cognizants Technology Solutions India Private Ltd., for an annual total package of Rs.3,35,000/-
along with other benefits and was ready to join.

entities.text: Cognizants Technology Solutions India Private Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to loss of deceased Ananda Kumar, his father and mother have come forward with the claim petition seeking a compensation for a sum of Rs.50,00,000/-.
4.1. The first respondent is the driver, the second respondent is the owner and the third respondent is the insurer of the lorry bearing Registration No. TN-33-BA-6945.
The fourth respondent is the owner and the fifth respondent is the insurer of the Tavera car bearing Registration No.TN-66-E-9927.
The first, second and fourth respondent have not contested the claim and remained ex-parte.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.2.

The lorry and Tavera car are insured with the same insurance company United India India Insurance Co. Ltd., and in the claim petition they are represented as third and fifth respondent respectively, hence the third respondent has filed a counter which is adopted by the fifth respondent.

entities.text: United India India Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The insurance company has contended the manner in which the accident was taken place and disputed the income, age, employment of the deceased and dependency of the claimants.

The insurance company has not raised the ground of violation of policy conditions but contended that the compensation claimed under various heads are on the higher side, hence prays to dismiss the claim petition.

5. Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimants, P.W.1 to P.W.4 were examined and Exs. P.1 to P.18 were marked and on the side of the respondents no witnesses were examined and no documents were marked.
On request of the claimants, additional Exs.X.1 to X.3, were marked through P.W.4.

Subbiramaniyam vs S. Sakthivel on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143668803/
2

6. Based on the evidence placed on record, the Tribunal in point https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis no.1, has held that the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the lorry, the first respondent is responsible for the accident.
In point no.2, the Tribunal has quantified and granted compensation for a sum of Rs.33,12,500/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition till the date of realisation.

7. Aggrieved over the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants have come forward with this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation on the ground that the Tribunal has not properly fixed compensation under the head loss of income.

8. The learned counsel appearing for the claimants has submitted that before the Tribunal, the claimants have examined three witnesses, who are working in the FACE academy to prove the avocation and income of the deceased and these evidences were not properly appreciated by the Tribunal, even though, the Tribunal has accepted that the deceased was engaged by FACE Academy but has not agreed with the income stated in the appointment order, which is marked as Ex.P.14 and fixed notional income of the deceased as Rs.20,000/- per month, which is not in accordance with the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis evidence placed on record, hence prays to modify the same.

9. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the insurance company has submitted that the evidence adduced more particularly the Ex.P.14 - Salary appointment order, is not sufficient to accept the income or salary earned by the deceased, hence the Tribunal has taken a view that his income would be treated as Rs.20,000/- per month, hence prays to confirm the same.

10. Heard the submissions on both sides and perused the materials placed on record.
10.1.

To prove the income of the deceased, the claimants have examined P.W.2, who is the Administrative Manager of the FACE Academy and he has stated that he is the manager and employed 300 persons in the academy and the persons are engaged by him as Consultant Trainee and their nature of job is to go various places and train the college student,

the deceased was also engaged as a Consultant Trainee in the academy on 08.06.2012 but unfortunately, before completing one month, the deceased https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Ananda Kumar died in the road accident.

The claimants have also marked Ex.P.14 through P.W.2, which is the confirmation letter as a Consultant Trainee from 08.06.2012 and the deceased was entitled to Rs.24,800/- as consulting fee per month and further stated that the deceased Ananda Kumar was regular in his employment and their institution is a private institution and they are also paying service tax.

10.2. The claimants have also examined P.W.4, who is Associate Admin. of the academy and through him Ex.X.3 was marked, which shows the nature of work and the nature of work attended by the deceased Ananda Kumar during the relevant working period.

On perusal of the same, it shows that,
the deceased Ananda Kumar has been deputed to various colleges to provide training to the student.
10.3.
Apart from P.W.2 and P.W.4, the person who worked along with the deceased Ananda Kumar was also examined as P.W.3, who also accompanied with the deceased in the car at the time of the accident.

P.W.3 is the eye witness to the occurrence and deposed about the nature of the work Subbiramaniyam vs S. Sakthivel on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143668803/
3 carried out by the deceased.

Combined evidence of P.W.2 to P.W.4 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis reveals that the deceased was engaged by the FACE Academy in contract basis and has a monthly consultancy pay of Rs.24,800/-.
11.

The Tribunal has accepted the above evidence and held that the deceased was working at the time of his death in the FACE Academy but the Tribunal has not accepted the consultancy fees received by him on monthly, offer letter has not specifically stated the salary structure, but the same was termed as Consultancy fees.
The evidence of P.W.2 and P.W.4 shows that this fees is revisable and other persons appointed along with the deceased also earning the very same amount.
Even though it is termed as a contract fees, it shall be termed as a regular monthly income.

Having accepted the employment of the deceased, the Tribunal ought to have accepted the consultancy fees to the deceased shall be fixed as the income of the deceased and accordingly, this Court is inclined to modify the monthly income of Rs.20,000/- to Rs.24,800/- in accordance with Ex.P.14.
12.

The Tribunal has fixed 50% as future prospectus for the deceased, but the deceased herein was working only as a consultant trainee and he was in the training period at the time of occurrance, he was not made https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis permanent,

hence as per the dictum as laid down in National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi case reported in 2017(2) TN MAC 609 (SC), the future prospectus of the deceased is fixed as 40% and as per Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 SC : 2009 (6) SCC 121, the multiplier is fixed as '18' by considering the age of the deceased at the time of the accident.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi case reported in 2017(2) TN MAC 609 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 SC : 2009 (6) SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of the evidence placed on record, the deceased is aged about 22 years at the time of accident, hence, this Court finds no infirmity in the above multiplier adopted by the Tribunal.

Since the deceased is a bachelor,  of his monthly income towards his personal and living expenses, as decided in Sarala Varma's case, the compensation under loss of income / dependency is assessed as follows:
Annual income (Rs.24,800/- x 12) = Rs.2,97,600/-
 Future prospects @40% = Rs.1,19,040/-
Yearly income of the deceased = Rs.4,16,640/-

Yearly contribution to his family = Rs.2,08,320/-
 Applicable Multiplier = 18

Total compensation (Rs.2,08,320/- x 18) = Rs.37,49,760/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 13.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- each towards love and affection to the claimants, who are the parents of the deceased, this Court is inclined to modify the same to Rs.40,000/- to each of the claimants and also modify the compensation granted under the head love and affection to loss of filial consortium as per the Subbiramaniyam vs S. Sakthivel on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143668803/
4
Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., vs Nanu Ram reported in 2018 ACJ 2018.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., vs Nanu Ram reported in 2018 ACJ 2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are entitled to get compensation under the conventional heads such as loss of estate and funeral expenses and this Court is inclined to modify the compensation of Rs.10,000/- awarded towards funeral expenses to Rs.15,000/- and Rs.2,500/- awarded towards loss of estate to Rs.15,000/-.
The funeral expenses awarded herein is inclusive of Transport charges.
Hence, the compensation awarded under head Transportation is rejected.

14. Accordingly, the award passed by the Tribunal under various heads are hereby modified as follows:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis S.

Description Amount Amount Award No awarded by awarded by confirmed or Tribunal this Court enhanced or (Rs) (Rs) reduced 1. Loss of income 32,40,000/- 37,49,760/- Confirmed 2. loss of consortium --- 80,000/- Granted

3. Love and affection 50,000/- --- Granted under consortium 4. Funeral expenses 10,000/- 15,000/- Enhanced 5. Transportation 10,000/- --- Rejected 6. Loss of estate 2,500/- 15,000/- Enhanced Compensation 33,12,500/- 38,59,760/-
Enhanced Awarded 18.

In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.33,12,500/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.38,59,760/- [Rupees Thiry Eight Lakhs Fifty Nine Thousand Seven Hundred and Sixty only] together along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of Claim Petition till the date of deposit, excluding the default period, if any.

The Respondent -Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount awarded by this Court along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.09 of 2013 on the file of the IV https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Additional District Judge, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Erode District at Bhavani.

entities.label: COURT

Since this Court has enhanced the compensation, the appellants/claimants are directed to pay the necessary Court fee, if any, on the enhanced compensation.
There shall be no order as to costs in the present appeal.
